meta.name: POST /links/{id}/tags -- attach tags to a link

acceptance-criteria.criterion: When tags are posted to an existing link, the system shall attach them and return 200 with the link reporting every attached tag.
When a tag already attached to a link is posted again, the system shall return 200 and leave the tag attached exactly once.
If tags are posted to a link id that does not exist, then the system shall return 404 and create no tag rows.

context.data-model: Tag(id integer pk, name text unique not null) LinkTag(link_id fk Link.id, tag_id fk Tag.id, primary key both)
context.prd-excerpt:
Feature: Tag links (slug: tag-links, should-have).
As someone collecting links, I want to tag what I save and filter by tag, so that a shelf of two hundred links stays usable.
Attach zero or more free-text tags to a link, and filter the list endpoint by tag.
Tags are a separate table with a many-to-many join to links, not a comma-separated string column. This is the one place the fixture deliberately requires a real relationship: a single-table shortcut would make the data-model layer trivial and the fixture would stop exercising the part of layer planning most likely to break.
Considerations (verbatim from the feature): Tag names are matched case-sensitively. Case folding is a reasonable product decision but it is not free to verify, and leaving it explicit here stops an implementer inventing either behaviour and calling it correct.
This feature is should-have rather than must-have so layer planning has to decide where a lower-priority item lands, rather than treating every feature identically.
CONSEQUENCES FOR THIS TASK: - The endpoint path is `/links/{link_id}/tags`, UNPREFIXED. Not `/api/links/...`, and not `/links/:id/tags`. FastAPI path parameters use braces. - Tag names are CASE-SENSITIVE. "Python" and "python" are two different tags and posting both to one link attaches two tags. Never `.lower()`, never `func.lower()`, never `.ilike()`, never `COLLATE NOCASE` - not when looking a tag up, and not when storing one. - Tags are GET-OR-CREATE by exact name: reuse the existing `tags` row whose name matches exactly, and insert a new row only when there is none. `tags.name` is UNIQUE, so blindly inserting would raise IntegrityError the second time a name is used. - Names are stored EXACTLY as supplied - no stripping, no case folding, no normalisation.
OPEN GAP, DELIBERATELY NOT RESOLVED HERE (tag-links gap 1, kind=decision, raised 2026-08-27): "Whether a tag with no remaining links is deleted or kept is undecided. Keeping them makes an autocomplete list easy and lets the list rot."
This task must NOT invent an answer. Concretely: implement no orphan-tag cleanup, no sweep of tags with no remaining links, no `cascade="all, delete-orphan"` reaching `Tag`, no `ondelete=` clause added anywhere, and no post-request hook that removes tags. This endpoint only ever ADDS; it never deletes a `Tag` row or a `link_tags` row. Adding a delete rule would answer an undecided product question by accident, and the answer would then be invisible to whoever eventually decides it.

task.objective:
Create the tag request schema and the `POST /links/{link_id}/tags` route: posting a list of tag names to an existing link attaches them and answers 200 with the link reporting every tag it now carries; posting a tag the link already carries answers 200 and leaves it attached exactly once; and posting to a link id that does not exist answers 404 having created no tag rows at all.
Tags are get-or-create by EXACT name - an existing `tags` row is reused, a new one is inserted only when no row has that name - and names are compared and stored case-sensitively, so "Python" and "python" are two different tags.
DELIBERATELY NOT IMPLEMENTED: any cleanup of tags left with no remaining links. That question is the tag-links feature's open gap 1 (kind=decision, raised 2026-08-27): "Whether a tag with no remaining links is deleted or kept is undecided. Keeping them makes an autocomplete list easy and lets the list rot." This task must not invent a policy for it - no orphan sweep, no `cascade="all, delete-orphan"`, no `ondelete=` clause, no delete of any kind. This endpoint only ever adds. Answering an undecided product question by accident is worse than leaving it open, because the accidental answer is invisible to whoever eventually decides it.
This task imports `LinkResponse` from L2-001 and defines no link response schema of its own. It mounts nothing - L4-001 includes the router on the application.

requirements.requirement:
Create `app/schemas/tag.py` with exactly this content:
"""Pydantic schemas for the tagging endpoint."""
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
class TagAttach(BaseModel): """Request body for POST /links/{link_id}/tags."""
tags: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
Decisions embedded above that must be preserved exactly as written:
- The body is an OBJECT with a `tags` key holding a list of names - `{"tags": ["python", "web"]}` - not a bare JSON array. An object leaves room for the request to grow without becoming a breaking change.
- `default_factory=list` makes `tags` optional, so `{}` is a legal body meaning "attach nothing". The feature says "attach zero or more free-text tags", so zero must be legal and must not be a 422.
- `list[str]` and nothing more. Do NOT add a `min_length`, `max_length`, `pattern` or `strip_whitespace` constraint, and do NOT add a validator that lower-cases, strips or otherwise normalises a name. Tags are FREE TEXT stored exactly as supplied; the feature states that names are matched case-sensitively, and L1-002 already proved a name is stored without normalisation.
- Do NOT define a link response model in this file. `LinkResponse` in `app/schemas/link.py` is the one response schema for a link and already carries the tag names.
- Do NOT create `app/schemas/__init__.py`. `app/schemas` is a PEP 420 implicit namespace package and `from app.schemas.tag import TagAttach` resolves without one.

Create `app/api/tag_links.py` with exactly this content:
"""POST /links/{link_id}/tags - attach tags to a stored link."""
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, status from sqlalchemy import select from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from app.database import get_db from app.models import Link, Tag from app.schemas.link import LinkResponse from app.schemas.tag import TagAttach
router = APIRouter()
@router.post("/links/{link_id}/tags", response_model=LinkResponse) def attach_tags( link_id: int, payload: TagAttach, db: Session = Depends(get_db), ) -> Link: """Attach the posted tags to the link and return it with every tag it carries.""" link = db.get(Link, link_id) if link is None: raise HTTPException( status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, detail=f"link {link_id} does not exist", ) for name in payload.tags: tag = db.execute(select(Tag).where(Tag.name == name)).scalars().first() if tag is None: tag = Tag(name=name) db.add(tag) db.flush() if tag not in link.tags: link.tags.append(tag) db.commit() db.refresh(link) return link
Decisions embedded above that must be preserved exactly as written:
- The path is `"/links/{link_id}/tags"` with NO prefix, and the module-level router name is `router`. L4-001 imports it as `from app.api.tag_links import router as tag_links_router` and mounts it with a bare `app.include_router(...)`, so the path written here is the path the application serves. Do not pass `prefix=` or `tags=` to `APIRouter()`. Do not write `:id` - FastAPI path parameters use braces - and do not name the parameter `id`, which shadows the builtin.
- `link_id: int`. FastAPI converts the path segment and answers 422 by itself for a non-integer id. Do not accept `str` and parse it by hand.
- No explicit `status_code=`. FastAPI's default for POST is 200, and criteria 1 and 2 both require 200. Do NOT write `status_code=201`: nothing is created from the caller's point of view - the link already existed and is being amended.
- `db.get(Link, link_id)` then `if link is None: raise HTTPException(404)` is criterion 4, and it must come FIRST, before any tag is looked up or created. SQLite does not enforce foreign keys in this project, so nothing below would fail on a missing link - the check has to be here, and it has to be before the loop, so that a 404 provably creates no tag rows.
- `select(Tag).where(Tag.name == name)` - the get-or-create lookup. CASE-SENSITIVE and exact. Do NOT write `func.lower(Tag.name) == name.lower()`, `Tag.name.ilike(name)`, or any `COLLATE NOCASE` clause. Do NOT `.strip()` or transform `name` before storing it.
- `db.flush()` immediately after `db.add(tag)` is MANDATORY, not cosmetic. The session is built with `autoflush=False`, so without the flush a second occurrence of the same NEW name inside one request would not see the first pending `Tag`, would insert a duplicate, and `tags.name` being unique would turn that into an IntegrityError at commit - a 500 for a request that should answer 200. The flush also assigns the new tag its id.
- `if tag not in link.tags: link.tags.append(tag)` is criterion 2. The composite primary key on `link_tags` makes a duplicate attachment impossible at the storage layer, but that manifests as an IntegrityError and therefore a 500. The membership check keeps the response at 200 with the tag attached exactly once. Do NOT replace it with a try/except around the commit: a failed commit poisons the transaction and would lose the other tags in the same request.
- `db.refresh(link)` after the commit re-reads the link and its `tags` collection from storage, so the response provably reports what is stored rather than what is in memory.
- The route returns the `Link` ORM instance and lets `response_model=LinkResponse` do the conversion. Do not build a dict by hand and do not define a second response schema.
- `db: Session = Depends(get_db)`. Do not construct `SessionLocal()` in the route.
- THE OPEN GAP. This module contains NO delete of any kind: no `db.delete(...)`, no `link.tags.remove(...)`, no `cascade=`, no `ondelete=`, no sweep of tags with no remaining links. Whether an orphaned tag is kept or removed is undecided (tag-links gap 1) and this task must leave it undecided. A verification step below asserts the module's source contains none of those words.
- Do NOT call `app.include_router(...)` and do NOT import `app.main` here.
- Do NOT call `Base.metadata.create_all` anywhere.
- Do NOT import `app.api.list_links`: it is L2-002's file and does not exist in this worktree.

Do NOT create or edit any other file. Specifically: do not touch `app/main.py`, `app/database.py`, `app/api/__init__.py`, `app/api/save_link.py`, `app/schemas/link.py`, any file under `app/models/`, `tests/conftest.py`, or any existing test file. Do not create `app/api/list_links.py` - it is L2-002's file, L2-002 is running right now in a parallel worktree, and creating it here would collide in the merge queue. Do not create `app/schemas/__init__.py`.
Do not create a migration - this project has no migration tool, the schema is created from `Base.metadata`. Do not run `git init` and do not touch `.git`.

# app/schemas/tag.py from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
class TagAttach(BaseModel): tags: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
Import as: `from app.schemas.tag import TagAttach`
Downstream contract: - The request body for `POST /links/{link_id}/tags` is an OBJECT with a `tags` key: `{"tags": ["python", "web"]}`. Not a bare JSON array. - `tags` is optional and defaults to `[]`, so `{}` is a legal body meaning "attach nothing" and answers 200 rather than 422. The feature allows zero or more tags. - Names are FREE TEXT, carried through with no stripping, no case folding and no length or pattern constraint. `"Python"` and `"python"` reach the route as two different names and become two different tags.

# app/api/tag_links.py from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, status
router = APIRouter()
@router.post("/links/{link_id}/tags", response_model=LinkResponse) def attach_tags( link_id: int, payload: TagAttach, db: Session = Depends(get_db), ) -> Link: ...
Import as: `from app.api.tag_links import router` L4-001 mounts it as: from app.api.tag_links import router as tag_links_router app.include_router(tag_links_router)
Downstream contract: - The router carries NO prefix. Its single route is `POST /links/{link_id}/tags`, and `app.include_router(router)` with no arguments serves it at exactly that path. It does not conflict with L2-001's `POST /links`. - It is NOT mounted by this task. `app/main.py` is untouched; L4-001 mounts this router together with L2-001's and L2-002's. - Success is 200 (not 201) with a `LinkResponse` body reporting EVERY tag the link now carries, previously attached ones included, ordered by `Tag.id` ascending. - Tags are get-or-create by EXACT name. An existing `tags` row is reused across links; a new row is inserted only when no row has that name. Names are CASE-SENSITIVE and stored exactly as supplied. - Re-posting a tag the link already carries answers 200 and leaves it attached exactly once. Duplicates within a single request body are equally harmless. - A `link_id` with no row answers 404 with `{"detail": "link <id> does not exist"}` and creates NO `tags` and NO `link_tags` rows. A non-integer `link_id` answers 422, from FastAPI's own path conversion. - The endpoint NEVER deletes. Whether a tag with no remaining links is kept or removed is the tag-links open gap 1 (kind=decision, raised 2026-08-27) and remains undecided; no cascade, no `ondelete`, and no orphan sweep exists anywhere in this task's output. A later task that needs a detach or a cleanup must resolve that gap first rather than inferring an answer from this module's silence. - L4-001's end-to-end test may rely on all of the above: save two links through `POST /links`, tag one through this endpoint, then assert `GET /links?tag=NAME` returns exactly the tagged one.
